para1: Every fighter has a Billy Presley story in him. The comeback fight nobody needed but everybody wanted tickets for.
para2: This week I'm running through Spider-Man's midlife crisis, Nolan turning The Odyssey into an endurance event, and a dinosaur movie that plays like interval training with teeth. But the real work is on Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, Jane Schoenbrun's meta-slasher about a director dragging her film's original final girl back for one more round decades later. I dig into why that setup nails something boxing gyms know cold: nobody pays to see you healed, they pay to see you reopened. Your scar tissue becomes the ticket price, and the people calling you back in are rarely villains, just fellow journeymen who never got out either.
